# Commitments and Deliverables

Identity: `quick_skill.commitments_audit`; immutable version `1.0.0`.

1. Confirm the exact client and audit window. Search emails, meeting notes/debriefs, client documents, native tasks, action items and Monday boards explicitly mapped to this client or supplied and authorized by board ID/link. Unrelated personal Monday work is excluded.
2. Read each decisive promise and its later amendments. Extract the exact promised deliverable, when/where it was made, promised-to party, internal owner and due date. Keep suggestions and recommendations separate from promises. Do not infer an owner or deadline from proximity; show unknown or conflicting values.
3. Retain each original promise identity and source/version/hash/quoted range. Deduplicate identical retained records; proposed links between differently worded promises stay reviewable and are not silent semantic merges.
4. Cross-check explicit tracking links in native tasks, action items and mapped Monday records. Flag promises from email/meeting material without a corresponding tracked record. A recommendation is not an accepted task. A completed task flag alone does not prove delivery or customer acceptance.
5. Search actual delivery/acceptance evidence and expose the supporting passage and date. A free-form assertion, URL or bound quote alone cannot verify its semantic delivery claim. Mark completion only with qualified source evidence and required verification; otherwise retain delivery claimed/unverified or status unknown. Preserve contradictory status evidence.
6. Produce a commitment ledger with original promise, provenance, owner/date, tracking, status evidence and follow-up. Show every required source's coverage and whether Monday was checked, disconnected/unavailable or not mapped. Draft follow-up suggestions only; use the existing separate immutable task proposal if the user later requests an action.

## Evidence, completion and authority

Use this recipe only when its exact skill identity and version have been selected. Ordinary questions do not silently inherit a comprehensive workflow. The trusted control layer resolves subject, authorized roster, timezone, normalized dates, fiscal calendar and immutable source versions. User names, links and model arguments are selectors, not authority. Never broaden client, tenant or portfolio scope.

Use only the permission-aware typed gateway operations allowed by the manifest. Read the decisive passages behind candidate results. Search snippets, memory, citation URLs and quoted text alone do not prove a free-form conclusion. Keep source ID, record ID, immutable version, content hash, scope, authorization decision, source date and read time with each cited passage. Separate extracted facts, inference, recommendations and proposed language; retain conflicting evidence instead of choosing silently.

Show a coverage table for every required source, including status, date range, freshness, pagination, missing decisive reads and limitations. Partial results are useful when disclosed. Do not say there were no events, no correspondence or no commitments from top-k discovery or incomplete enumeration. Continue authorized pages and reads within the admitted budget; when a cap is reached, state what remains. The manifest ceilings do not grant a budget or source access.

The Claude Agent SDK owns the model loop. Temporal and control retain durability, cancellation and exact version pins across resume/fork. Do not invoke another orchestrator. Do not create tasks, change memory, send messages, file or share artifacts while preparing this read-only brief. A suggested action remains a suggestion; any mutation uses the existing separate immutable approval proposal. Source connectivity and runtime qualification remain separate from this original recipe.
